summary: Wicomico Co., MD steel lookout near Quantico: 1931 newspapers vs NHLR's 1941 date; moved in 1999 to the Chesapeake Fire Museum in Hebron; original site listed gone.

facts.design: Aermotor steel tower with a 7' x 7' metal cab and a 'widow's walk' roof (NHLR)
facts.status_note: Moved in 1999 to the Chesapeake Fire Museum in Hebron; the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the original Quantico site as gone
facts.agency: Maryland Forest Service built it (NHLR); the Chesapeake Fire Museum administers it (NHLR)

events.note: July 1931 newspaper: a 100-foot tower recently erected at Quantico; Forest Worker, September 1931: ready for service in July. Conflicts with the NHLR 1941 date
NHLR: constructed near Hebron in Wicomico County in 1941 by the Maryland Forest Service
Newspaper report of an April 23, 1942 fire at Hall's Swamp near Allen names towerman Marion Bailey of the Quantico lookout
Fire at Hall's Swamp near Allen, reported April 23, 1942; controlled after four hours, broke out again at noon
Used for fire detection and as an Aircraft Warning Service (AWS) site in World War II (NHLR; no year given)
Last staffed in the 1970s (NHLR; no exact year given)
State transferred ownership of the 0.60-acre Quantico tower site to the University of Maryland (DNR caption)
Tower moved to the Chesapeake Fire Museum, Hebron
Top 60 feet and cab reconstructed and restored at the museum
DNR report dated April 2007: tower now resides at Chesapeake Fire Museum, Hebron
Date registered March 1, 2000 as US 338, MD 1

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1931 newspapers describe a new 100-foot tower at Quantico; the NHLR dates construction to 1941. Both dates are kept as events and the story says the dates are disputed
The NHLR gives 140 feet (42.7 m); the 1931 newspaper says 100 feet. facts.height_m uses the NHLR figure and the story notes the difference
The 1931 report credits woodland owners and county commissioners; the NHLR says the federal government financed it. Not reconciled

The FFLA lists the original site as gone and the museum tower as standing. The NHLR entry names the museum as location but its coordinates (38.36211, -75.692624) match the original site, not the museum at 38.41445, -75.67551

notes_for_editor: Two accounts of the build date, height and funding conflict (1931 newspapers via Forest Lookouts vs NHLR 1941/140 ft/federal). Current access to the museum tower is not established: the museum's own site was not read and no visiting hours or climbing rules were found. No source describes what remains at the original site. No new photos found. Three searches were run for this lookout, one over the budget of two.
